title: Coherent reduction of the integral braiding scalar-extension square
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite coefficient fields $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with an algebra map $\iota:E\to L$, and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field. Let $S$ be the prescribed integral scalar-extension functor, $T_E,T_L$ the prescribed completed integral tensors, $\beta^E,\beta^L$ the coherently normalized integral braidings, and $\lambda^{\mathrm{int}}$ the prescribed tensor scalar comparison. For all $M,N$, the two composites
$$S(\beta^E_{M,N});\lambda^{\mathrm{int}}_{N,M},\qquad
\lambda^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,N};\beta^L_{S M,S N}$$
have equal images under the coherent reduction functor for coefficient field $L$. Equivalently, the coherent reductions of the two displayed morphisms from $S(T_E(M,N))$ to $T_L(SN,SM)$ are equal. This is the finite-stage signed-swap assertion used to prove the integral square; it is strictly weaker than equality before coherent reduction and imposes no additional hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ, signed total symmetry on homogeneous generators; coherent reduction form of the prescribed integral scalar-extension comparison

proof.text: Use the scalar tensor coherent-reduction square and the defining reduction equations of the two integral braidings. Naturality of the scalar reduction p moves the source braiding through p. Apply H to its tensor reduction equation, then use the whole-system scalar tensorator signed-symmetry square. Naturality of the target system braiding moves the two p components to the other side. Cancel the invertible target tensor reduction and tensor of p components. The generic reduced_braiding calculation performs this diagram chase; mapping its equality by coherent reduction gives the stated equality.
